verses.mystical_translation: A brief crown laid on the ground of the city; a people's choice, a throat of bread and breath.
Youth on a throne for a season counted by months; the city's clock runs down.
A treasury opened by foreign hand; the city's silver and gold measured as a price.
A name exchanged like a garment; one brother carried away, another clothed with a throne.
An eleven-year span marked by choices that closed the ear to the holy voice.
A foreign king rose like a tide and bound the house's bolt; a ruler led away in chains.
Sacred vessels travel to a foreign shrine; the house's treasures become trophies.
Annals record the deeds and the stain; the scroll of kings receives another hand on the throne.
A child on a shaken throne; short days counted under a stern sky.
When the year closed, the king's hand gathered throne and treasure; a brother placed as proxy.
An eleven-year doorway; a young man bearing years heavy as walls.
Prophetic words offered; the ear closed, the heart hardened, and the prophet's voice returned to silence.
An oath placed and broken; the neck set like iron, the heart turned away from the city’s covenant.
Those set to keep the holy became the agents of defilement; the sanctuary's veil is stained from within.
Compassion sent like dawn; the city received the repeated knocking of grace.
Mockery like a cord tightened until the spring breaks; the city’s medicine gone.
The Chaldean king entered; the sanctuary's threshold tasted sword, the remnant handed over as spoil.
Everything carried away: great and small, the palace and the sanctuary emptied into foreign storehouses.
Flame traced the city's shape; palaces and vessels collapse into ash and memory.
The remnant became house-servants in a foreign court, counted under another king's years.
The land kept a long Sabbath; desolation became a slow liturgy that fulfilled the prophet's word.
A foreign king's spirit quickened by the hand of the God of heaven; a written trumpet across the realms.
A decree like a key: permission to climb the long stair home; the God of heaven named as grantor of kingdom and command.

contemplative_note: Kings fall, vessels are taken, and exile becomes the land's Sabbath — the chapter closes with a royal summons that begins return and rebuilding.
safety_note: This chapter contains descriptions of violence, exile, and destruction retained from the source; use for study and historical-critical work only.
